fact: The BMJ Global Health study states that an assigned health worker at each public primary healthcare centre (CSPS) summarises service volumes on paper forms and submits them monthly to the district statistics team, which enters them into the online DHIS2 database; the study's DHIS2 data run from December 2017 to December 2021 and it dates the practice no more closely.

The study states that DHIS2 is implemented nationwide, including all CSPS facilities, the first level of a three-tier public system, as monthly reports keyed by the district; in its two districts report completeness was 100% (34 facilities, Toma) and 95.5% to 100% (36 facilities, Gourcy) over December 2017 to December 2021. It names no other tier.

The Ministry of Health's Plan stratégique de la santé numérique 2025-2029, dated January 2025 and drawn up by its Direction des systèmes d'information, names Endos-BF among the solutions already deployed and carries an axis on modernising the health information system; it is costed at 42,576,806,267 FCFA, against 2,762,824,725 FCFA of available funds and a financing gap of 39,813,981,543 FCFA.

The Ministry of Health's strategy lists, among innovations in the health system, the scaling-up of decentralised entry of routine data in health facilities; it gives no count of facilities and no date, so the document's date is used, and it does not name the system in that sentence.
